about: Four rail_access topics, one city each: the Rail Access Monitor's starting cities (docs/enhancements/rail-access-monitor.md §2). Each entry is a complete body for the admin API's POST /topics; docs/deployment-runsheet.md, 'rail_access topics', shows how to create them with scripts/admin_cli.py. Each box sits inside one 100 km UTM square, so inside one Sentinel-2 tile. adapter_config sets only the site and its reach, and for Sydney the 80 s time_budget_seconds cap (its first OpenStreetMap network takes most of a minute: docs/deployment-runsheet.md, 'rail_access topics'); every other key takes the rail_access adapter's default (docs/enhancements/vision.md §5). The cities take turns, one a day, each at 09:05 Sydney time: Sydney on Monday and Friday, Melbourne on Tuesday and Saturday, Singapore on Wednesday and Sunday, Boston on Thursday. Each article drafts every Finding made since that city's last article. findings_window_hours is 192 (8 days): Boston's 7 days between runs, the longest gap, plus a day for a clock change or a late run. The window never reaches back past the city's last article, so no Finding is drafted twice. A day with no new Finding stops before any model call. Adding a city means adding a topic on a day of its own (one of a two-day city's days) or on a day it shares with another city; 192 hours covers any city that runs at least once a week. force_manual_review is forced on for this adapter whether or not it is sent.

editorial_goals.primary_focus: Report what the rail access measurements show for Sydney: the share of its built-up area within walking reach of a rail station, the built-up area beyond it, the station count, the scene's capture date and coverage, and the rule-based flags and simulations, as proxies measured from satellite imagery and OpenStreetMap.
editorial_goals.exclusion_criteria: No ridership, timetable, journey time, cost or funding claims; no recommendation to build, extend or close anything; no cause, forecast, political or planning view; no place names or numbers that are not in the findings.
